narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate that oil contributes a negligible portion to Dubai's GDP today.

units.meaning: Oil accounts for 0.3% of Dubai's GDP, below the 1% threshold — a negligible share.

basis.note: Table value is 0.3 in % units; relative_value 0.003 confirms 0.3%.

accepted_routes: Oil's share of GDP is about 0.3%.
Oil contributes roughly one-third of one percent of GDP.
Oil accounts for less than 1% of GDP.
Oil's GDP share is below one percent.
Not even 1% of Dubai's GDP comes from oil.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The oil slice/segment or an on-screen label must display 0.3% (or 'about 0.3%' / 'less than 1%') as the oil share of GDP.
units.temporal_anchor: today it only accounts for ... of its GDP
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the exact 0.3% oil share, or is the <1% threshold sufficient?

basis.note: Table value is 99.7 in % units; relative_value 0.997 confirms 99.7%.

accepted_routes: The rest of Dubai's GDP accounts for 99.7%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The non-oil slice or complement label must display 99.7%, or the chart must clearly show the rest of the pie making up nearly all GDP.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly give the non-oil complement value, or is showing only oil's tiny share enough?

optional_valid: Dubai does have oil, but it is a tiny GDP category; this identity statement is valid only if it is not confused with oil being a large share.
A visual 1% benchmark line is optional if the text already clearly says oil is less than 1%.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims about economic diversification or oil causing non-oil growth.
Historical trends, future projections, or dates not in the table.
Dollar GDP amounts, total GDP figures, or other sector breakdowns.
Saying oil is 0% of GDP or that Dubai has no oil.
Comparing oil to non-oil GDP using the wrong denominator, e.g., 0.3% of non-oil GDP.
Claiming oil is exactly 1% of GDP.
notes: The table gives only two shares, so all numeric claims should stay within 0.3%, 99.7%, and derived <1%, 99.4 pp, ~332x, or 100% sum. Do not add years, GDP dollar amounts, other sectors, or causal claims about diversification.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only

trim.reason: 人工指定：U1 与 U2 合并（0.3% 与低于 1% 是同一个事实）
